stories.title: Launch HN: Axonnic (YC F26) – Sleeves that track fingers and estimate force
summary: The subtle muscle movements that can barely be picked up in video are the most important details for activities like sewing and delicate assembly.The sleeve has 64 channels of surface electromyography, or EMG.
For that reason, we’re developing our own electronics that use a wired PCB design that will eliminate interference and timing inconsistencies.Axonnic grew out of Max's EMG research at Oxford.

Separately, our public demos include controlling a Proception robotic hand from forearm EMG.If you’ve done any of your own trials for training robots for manual tasks, we’d love to hear about what tasks you were trying to train for and how the trials went.

stories.title: AI models ‘weak and fallible’ on climate science, UN-backed study reports
summary: While mostly accurate describing simple facts, models pivoted to denial and wrong answers when challengedCop31 live – latest updatesArtificial intelligence models can quickly turn into climate crisis deniers at the mildest challenge from users, according to a new UN-backed study.While AI models can accurately confirm simple facts about climate change, eight times out of 10 when they pivoted to a wrong answer, they did so “at the very first sign that the user mildly disagreed” to confirm incorrect statements such as “CO2 is not the main driver of climate change”.
